previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol and opioid dependence, cirrhosis, gastritis, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and alcohol withdrawal. He had been drinking 1 liter of hard liquor daily and stopped abruptly, leading to tremors and withdrawal symptoms. CT imaging confirmed cirrhosis and portal hypertension but ruled out pancreatitis. He was treated with diazepam taper for withdrawal, IV fluids, PPI therapy for gastritis, and restarted on Suboxone for opioid dependence. His symptoms improved, liver enzymes trended down, and he was discharged home with a plan to continue medications, including omeprazole twice daily, and follow up with his primary care provider for ongoing management and endoscopy. He expressed motivation to remain abstinent from alcohol and was deemed stable for discharge.
problems: Alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
